parts.part: whole town (citadel and lower town within one fortification)
parts.layout_phase: Period IIA, Early Mature Harappan (Rao et al. 2005, 2006), the 'Period II: Transitional' of the 2003-04 report
parts.what_was_built: The first fortified and planned town at Bhirrana belongs to Period IIA. The 2005-06 report states that 'the entire settlement was reorganized' in this period, that 'the complete town was encompassed within a fortification wall as indicated by the partially traced wall lying underneath the northern and western arms of the fortification wall of the Mature Harappan period', and that 'the concept of twin units of town planning, viz. Citadel and Lower Town also came up during this period', the citadel in the west-north-west part of the mound and the lower town in the east-south-east, separated by a mud-brick wall 2.70 m wide, with the main entrances in the middle of the walls and a fortified lower town (Rao et al. 2006: 47-48). The preceding Period IB 'was probably an unfortified settlement as no defence/fortification wall has come to light so far' (p. 47). In Period IIB the Mature Harappans 'strengthened and enhanced the height of the wall' with yellowish mud bricks, moved the main entrances to the corners and partially modified the layout; streets of that period are 2.80 m wide in the lower town and 4.0 m in the citadel, with a thoroughfare about 4.10 m wide along the wall (pp. 48-49). The wall exposed in 2004-05 is of mud brick in the ratio 1:2:4, 95 m long, 5 m wide, seventeen courses and 1.80 m high on its northern side, and 2.50-2.75 m wide on its southern side (Rao et al. 2005: 63-64).
parts.locator: rao2006bhirrana pp. 47-49; rao2005bhirrana pp. 60, 63-64; rao2004bhirrana p. 21
parts.excavator_basis: Radiocarbon. The excavators' own reports give no calendar range for Period IIA: Rao et al. 2005: 67 say only that four BSIP dates agree with the known Harappan chronology from 'the fag end of the 4th millennium to the middle of the 2nd millennium BC' while three are 'very early'. The range 4500-3000 BCE for IIA ('Beginning of fortification wall, house-complexes, streets and lanes') is printed in the supplement of Sarkar et al. 2016 (p. 3), co-authored by the excavator L. S. Rao, 'based on radiocarbon ages in different trenches' and compiled from Rao et al. 2004-05 and Dikshit and Mani 2012; Dikshit 2022: 173 gives the same bracket, 'IIA C. 4500-3000 BCE'.

radiocarbon.note: The supplement prints the radiocarbon age only as '4170 ± 250' in a column headed '14C age±1 year BC', states that 'all 14C ages are based on a half life of 5.730± 40 year', and cites Mani 2008 for the dates; it gives no period for the sample. 4170 BC is 1950 years less than the 6120 BP printed by Rao et al. 2005, so if Sarkar et al. are right the BSIP ages are on the 5730-year half-life and the 5568-year equivalent of 6120 ± 250 would be about 5942 ± 243 (our arithmetic; the published calibrations use the printed age unchanged).

syntheses.statement: Describes 'the fortification wall of Early Mature Harappan (IIA) and Mature Harappan (IIB)' and prints nineteen BSIP dates, which he groups by calibrated range into IA c. 7500-6000, IB c. 6000-4500, IIA c. 4500-3000, IIB c. 3000-1800 and IIC to c. 1600 BCE; in his own scheme the IIA group is 'Period IIB (Early Harappan)'.
syntheses.disagreement: Calls the dates of the excavator's Early Mature Harappan IIA 'Early Harappan', and his calendar conversions of the same BSIP ages differ from those of Rao et al. 2005.

syntheses.statement: Gives the Bhirrana sequence as 'Pre-Harappan Hakra phase (~9.5–8 ka BP), Early Harappan (~8–6.5 ka BP), Early mature Harappan (~6.5–5 ka BP) and mature Harappan (~5–2.8 ka BP)', and reports an OSL age of 5.9 ± 0.25 ka BP (6185 to 5695 years BP) for pottery from the early mature Harappan level at 143 cm in trench YF-2 and 4.8 ± 0.3 ka BP for mature Harappan pottery at 42 cm, which it takes as confirming the radiocarbon chronology.
syntheses.disagreement: Its early mature Harappan bracket (about 4550-3050 BCE in calendar terms) and the OSL age put the layout some two millennia before the conventional start of the Mature Harappan about 2600 BCE.

parts.conflicts: The excavators changed their attribution of the first wall. In 2003-04 'the town appears to have been fortified' in Period II, then called Transitional, 'which needs to be confirmed' (Rao et al. 2004: 21); in 2004-05 the fortification was described under Period IIb, Mature Harappan, and little was found of IIa (Rao et al. 2005: 63); in 2005-06 the first wall and the division into citadel and lower town were assigned to IIA, with IIB strengthening them (Rao et al. 2006: 47-48). The radiocarbon evidence has no published contexts except four dates in Sarkar et al. 2016, which give trench and depth but no period. Two different samples carry the label BRN 6 (BS-2333 and BS-2482). Sarkar et al. state that the BSIP ages are on the 5730-year half-life, while Rao et al. and Dikshit state no half-life, and the BCE conversions of the same ages differ between Rao et al. 2005 and Dikshit 2022. The dates Dikshit assigns to IIA (about 4700-2700 BCE) are far older than conventional Mature Harappan dates, a point the excavators themselves flagged as needing confirmation.

first_occupation.phase: Period IA, Hakra Ware Culture: subterranean dwelling pits cut into natural soil
first_occupation.basis: Radiocarbon. The earliest BSIP dates are BS-2333 (BRN 6, 7590 ± 240 BP, 8597-8171 BP, 6647-6221 BC; Rao et al. 2005: 67) and BS-2481 (BRN 9, 8350 ± 140 BP, 7570-7180 BCE; Dikshit 2022: 172); the range 7500-6000 BCE for IA is printed in the supplement of Sarkar et al. 2016 (p. 3), co-authored by the excavator, and in Dikshit 2022: 172 ('IA C. 7500-6000 BCE'). Rao et al. 2005: 67 treated the earliest dates as needing confirmation.

notes:
Bhirrana (Fatehabad district) is a mound of about 190 x 150 m and 5.5 m high, excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India under L. S. Rao from 2003 to 2006 (Rao et al. 2004: 20). The excavators' sequence, as revised in 2004-05, is Period IA (Hakra Ware Culture, dwelling pits), IB (Early Harappan), IIA (Early Mature Harappan) and IIB (Mature Harappan) (Rao et al. 2005: 60); the first report's 'Period II: Transitional' became IIA. We read the three interim reports in Puratattva 34, 35 and 36; the Puratattva 34 and 35 copies are locally held image scans, which we read from their page images.

We list radiocarbon dates only where a published source ties them to IIA or IB: two in Rao et al. 2005 that Dikshit later grouped with those periods, one in Sarkar et al. 2016 with trench and depth, and Dikshit's grouped dates. Dikshit's period assignments are made by calibrated date, not by context, so they cannot test the chronology on their own. The BSIP date lists for Bhirrana have never appeared in Radiocarbon. No Bayesian model has been published. We did not obtain Mani 2008 or Dikshit and Mani 2012, which the supplement of Sarkar et al. cites as the source of its dates and periods, nor any final report of the excavation; the 2016 article in Heritage: Journal of Multidisciplinary Studies in Archaeology 4 that we checked concerns a seal from Bhirrana and gives no dates.
